output.myth: When Aun cut the string and the sky went up, he was thirsty, as Fliers are, having shouted all day at the wind. He had no bottle. Ennu the Kite-Wright sat on the cliff with a goatskin and a needle and said, Fool, you cannot carry water up a cliff with your mouth. So she sewed him a bag from one goat, with the neck tied off with cord and a strap long enough to reach the pasture. Aun slung it over his shoulder and set off along the Lamp Road. Tavo came down the wind and tried to take the cork, and laughed, and could not. The seams held. Some say the bag is still on him, and that the stitching shows when the road is long. Grandmother says that is why we sew the seams tight before every journey, and why we never ask the Gale how far. Fill the bag before you go, child. The road is longer than it looks.
output.verse:
Goatskin sewn and tied,
the long road makes the seams show,
fill it at the cliff.
